The most likely corrupted element is the tail current source M5. It has the largest UGBW sensitivity (+18.2%), it is at the edge of saturation (Vds-Vdsat = 0.042 V, gm/gds = 9.7), and its tail current is what sets gm1 and therefore UGBW and settling. Its mirror ratio against M6 checks out (about 2.26, giving 22.4 µA against the 10 µA reference), so the fault is more likely a size or length change that leaves M5 in a marginal operating region than a simple ratio error. M6 is second because it shares the same tail-current control, and M3 is third because it sets the load-side gm with a much smaller sensitivity.

{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M3"], "fault": "Tail current source M5 is sized/biased so that it operates at the edge of saturation (Vds-Vdsat about 0.04 V, gm/gds 9.7), which limits the tail current and gm1 and lowers UGBW and slows settling. The most likely cause is a corrupted W or L on M5."}
